[0] [0] [0] Folded screens typically develop more noticeable creases with extended use, but Apple's Kate Bergeron has stated that the dual-screen iPhone (Duo) employs a replaceable protective layer on the foldable screen to help mitigate this issue.

[1] [1] [1] The 'protective layer' on the dual-screen iPhone's foldable screen can be replaced over time, maintaining a like-new condition long-term

[2] [2] [2] Following the unveiling of the dual-screen iPhone last month, Apple executives gave interviews explaining why the company was so deliberate in maximizing durability and reducing the crease issues that plague other foldable devices.

[3] [3] [3] To achieve this goal, the dual-screen iPhone appears to incorporate a unique design that allows users to maintain a 'like-new' experience for years: the protective layer on the foldable screen is replaceable.

[4] [4] [4] Below is the interview with Apple's Vice President of Hardware Engineering, Kate Bergeron, conducted by TikTok user @angietutorials:

[5] [5] [5] A popular comment left by OrangeQuill

[6] [6] [6] Knowing that they felt the need to add this design makes me even more worried about how the device will hold up over time. Hopefully they're just being overly cautious, and hopefully the maintenance costs aren't outrageously expensive on top of having to pay for AppleCare separately

[7] [7] [7] You can watch the full interview clip on TikTok.

[8] [8] [8] Apple mentions this 'protective layer' in its estimated AppleCare repair cost chart for the dual-screen iPhone. Discovered by Quinn Nelson, the protective layer replacement cost with AppleCare is $19. The replacement cost without AppleCare is currently unclear.

[9] [9] [9] So if you're worried about the crease becoming more pronounced over time after spending over $2,000 on a dual-screen iPhone, it sounds like Apple already has a solution.

[10] [10] [10] Are you concerned about the crease issue on the dual-screen iPhone? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
